about: Extra powder phases a single-crystal volume can carry: flux metals, sample-environment metals and a few other common phases (nebula3d.preprocessing.powder_phases). Each entry gives its space group, a room-temperature cell with its source, and the atoms of the cell, from which the allowed reflections and their neutron intensities are computed. Cells and atoms are those of the Crystallography Open Database entry named (COD, https://www.crystallography.net/), whose original paper is cited. A site lists its coordinates; 'ops' (coordinate triplets) and 'centering' expand it to the whole cell. Add a phase with the same fields in a file of your own (load_library(extra=...), or the NEBULA3D_POWDER_PHASES environment variable).
about_broad: Broad-feature entries (polymer halos, for X-rays) go in 'broad': each {id, name, halos: [{q, fwhm} in Å⁻¹], source}, matched against the profile's broad excess and reported apart from the sharp rings. Kapton and GE varnish are not shipped yet: no halo centre and width could be taken from a source read for this library, and an entry must cite one. Add them in your own file once a source is chosen.

scattering_lengths.source: Bound coherent neutron scattering lengths (real part), V. F. Sears, Neutron News 3(3), 26-37 (1992), as tabulated by the NIST Center for Neutron Research
